title: An owned meaning is settled on sight; waiting at a gate is never holding it open
situation: An earlier ruling said the architect settles a meaning question it owns in any turn, and that holding it open for the operator is a hand-back. A fresh architect read it as a reason to record past the operator's read-back.
decision: The architect settles a meaning question it owns as soon as it holds what that needs, in any turn, and records the ruling before reporting it; it leaves open only a question that needs something it does not hold, and reports the one action that will get it. This governs meaning only. Recording is a change, so at a session's start, or where the operator has called a read-back before recording, the ruling is carried in the read-back and recorded only once the operator signs off. Waiting at a gate for the operator's sign-off is neither holding open nor a hand-back.
consequences: The drift and architect concepts state this; the rubrics of the earlier ruling keep reading a decision taken in the turn as that topic's outcome.
